name: Jenner’s cowpox-based vaccination
summary: Edward Jenner showed and published that deliberately giving people mild cowpox protected them against smallpox, the founding practice of vaccination.
description: A preventive vaccination approach documented by Jenner in 1796 and published from 1798; distinct from earlier smallpox variolation and other earlier cowpox practices.
tier_reason: The preventive approach underlies later vaccination programmes and generations of infectious-disease prevention, beyond a single experimental recipient.

impact.note: Vaccination reached most of humanity, is the depth 2 case in the scoring guide, and became the platform for immunology, vaccines and eradication over generations.

why: Smallpox was a leading killer, and country people in Gloucestershire held that milkmaids who caught cowpox escaped it.

date.basis: RCPE dates Jenner’s documented vaccination result to 1796; no worldwide first vaccination is inferred.
